title: Principal Research Scientist – Biomedical Engineering & Neurotechnology
description:
Biomedical Research Scientist

**Location:** Remote / Hybrid – United States. Candidates from Baltimore, Boston, Dallas, San Francisco, or Atlanta are encouraged to apply.

About the Opportunity

A privately held medical technology venture is seeking an exceptional doctoral-level researcher, PhD candidate, or experienced research scientist to lead advanced research and invention development.

We are developing next-generation medical and wellness technologies with a focus on neurological applications, advanced therapeutic systems, and innovative medical devices.

We are looking for a highly intelligent, creative, and technically accomplished scientist who can move beyond academic research to develop original inventions, design new technologies, and contribute to the creation of a valuable patent portfolio.

The ideal candidate has experience with scientific discovery, experimental research, prototype development, and the patent application process.

This opportunity is ideal for an entrepreneurial scientist who wants to help transform innovative concepts into proprietary technologies with significant commercial potential.

Primary Research Areas

We are particularly interested in expertise involving:

* Biomedical engineering and medical device invention
* Neuroscience and neuroengineering
* Alzheimer's disease and neurodegenerative disorders
* Neuromodulation and brain stimulation technologies
* Photobiomodulation and near-infrared light
* Pulsed electromagnetic field (PEMF) technologies
* Bioelectromagnetics and biophysics
* Frequency-based therapeutic technologies
* Multifunction therapeutic beds and advanced wellness systems
* Neuroplasticity and neurological rehabilitation
* Medical device integration and emerging therapeutic technologies

Key Responsibilities

**Scientific Research & Innovation**

* Conduct original scientific research into emerging biomedical and neurological technologies.
* Identify opportunities for new inventions and proprietary technologies.
* Design research studies, experiments, and technical feasibility assessments.
* Evaluate existing technologies, scientific publications, and clinical evidence.
* Develop innovative concepts for advanced medical devices and therapeutic systems.

**Patent Development & Intellectual Property**

* Identify potentially patentable inventions and technological improvements.
* Conduct preliminary patent landscape and prior-art research.
* Prepare technical invention disclosures, specifications, drawings, and supporting documentation.
* Collaborate with registered patent attorneys or patent agents to prepare and file patent applications.
* Support the development of provisional and nonprovisional patent applications.
* Help establish a long-term intellectual property development strategy.
* Identify opportunities for technology licensing and commercialization.

**Medical Device Development**

* Support the design and development of new medical technologies.
* Collaborate with engineers, inventors, and technical specialists.
* Participate in prototype development, testing, and validation.
* Evaluate technical feasibility, safety, and potential clinical applications.
* Support regulatory research and documentation related to medical device development.

Required Qualifications

* Currently pursuing or holding a PhD in Biomedical Engineering, Neuroscience, Electrical Engineering, Biophysics, Applied Physics, or a closely related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience conducting independent scientific research.
* Strong understanding of experimental design, technical documentation, and scientific methodology.
* Experience developing original technologies, inventions, or patentable innovations.
* Familiarity with intellectual property development and patent applications.
* Ability to translate scientific concepts into practical medical device applications.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and innovation capabilities.

Highly Preferred Qualifications

* Named inventor on one or more related patent applications or issued patents.
* Experience preparing invention disclosures or working directly with patent counsel.
* Previous involvement in medical device research and development.
* Experience with electromagnetic, photonic, or neurological technologies.
* Published scientific research in relevant fields.
* Experience taking technology from concept through prototype development.
* Familiarity with FDA medical device development requirements.
* Entrepreneurial experience or involvement in technology commercialization.

Ideal Candidate

We are looking for more than a traditional academic researcher.

Our ideal candidate is a scientist and inventor who:

* Thinks creatively and challenges conventional approaches.
* Has a demonstrated ability to develop original intellectual property.
* Understands both scientific research and commercial applications.
* Can independently lead complex technical research initiatives.
* Is excited about building a portfolio of patented technologies.
* Values integrity, collaboration, and meaningful scientific innovation.
* Wants to contribute to technologies that may improve human health and quality of life.

Opportunity & Growth

This position offers the opportunity to:

* Participate in the invention of next-generation medical devices.
* Lead research initiatives with significant commercial potential.
* Develop and contribute to a growing intellectual property portfolio.
* Collaborate with experienced entrepreneurs and technology commercialization professionals.
* Help shape the scientific direction of an emerging medical technology venture.
* Explore potential long-term scientific leadership opportunities.

Compensation will be based on qualifications, experience, and project scope. Potential long-term arrangements may include performance incentives or equity participation, subject to mutually agreed terms.

Confidentiality

This is a confidential opportunity. Additional information about the company, proprietary technologies, and specific research initiatives will be provided to qualified candidates during the interview process, subject to appropriate confidentiality agreements.

How to Apply

Please submit:

* Current CV or resume.
* Educational background and research specialization.
* Relevant scientific publications.
* Patent applications or issued patents on which you are a named inventor.
* Examples of original research, inventions, or medical device development projects.
* A brief description of your experience working with patent attorneys or preparing technical documentation for patent filings.

Pay: $78,400.00 - $119,000.00 per year

Work Location: Remote

title: Information Specialist III
description:
Overview:

**Information Specialist III**  
  
**Be Part of One Team, One Purpose.**  
  
At **Emmes Group**, we’re shaping the future of clinical research—**where human intelligence meets cutting-edge technology** to drive meaningful advancements in healthcare. With over **47 years of scientific excellence**, we’ve led groundbreaking research in **cell and gene therapy, vaccines, infectious diseases, ophthalmology, rare diseases, and neuroscience.**  
  
Through our two business units—**Emmes, a full-service CRO**, and **Veridix AI, our technology, data, and analytical solutions** —we are modernizing clinical trials and accelerating the development of life-changing therapies.  
  
We believe that every clinical breakthrough starts with **people**—people who are **passionate, purpose-driven, and ready to make an impact.** At **Emmes Group, we bring People, Science, and Technology together to collaborate with our customers and deliver global health impact.** Our culture is built on **integrity, collaboration, and innovation**, ensuring that every challenge is met with perseverance and accountability.

The Information Specialist Group is comprised of staff providing project management and informational support for cancer research. The Information Specialist III performs a variety of activities, including but not limited to project management for initiatives related to cancer clinical trials, including coordination of working groups and committees, tracking and reporting on progress of clinical trials and related studies, organizing calls/meetings, developing agendas and writing meeting minutes, compiling various information for clinical trialists and other cancer researchers, and following up on action items to advance the project.

Responsibilities:

* Provide project management and coordination for efforts related to cancer clinical research, including clinical trial development, clinical trial implementation and progress, correlative/biomarker studies, data- and specimen-sharing efforts, and other efforts for which the National Cancer Institute (NCI) requires support for its clinical trials portfolio.
* Coordinate working groups and committees of cancer researchers, including organizing meetings/calls, developing agendas and PowerPoint slides, and writing meeting minutes and action items. Calls/meetings include those with clinical investigators, laboratory scientists, pharmaceutical companies, biostatisticians, and other personnel involved in research studies.
* Identify and follow up on action items, including sending reminders, to keep projects on track, including conferring with project leadership and updating them on progress.
* Track and report on progress of clinical trials and related studies, which requires the ability to look up information on websites and in databases, inquire and communicate with project staff, and synthesize information into reports.
* Maintain trackers and a collaborative website where shared documents and communications are posted.
* Abstract, synthesize, review, and demonstrate understanding of information from cancer clinical trial protocol documents, cancer clinical trial manuscripts, literature searches, and cancer clinical trial databases.
* Create and maintain updated rosters.
* May contribute to scientific manuscripts and presentations.
* May maintain project websites.
* Demonstrates understanding of project and corporate Standard Operating Procedures SOPs by producing work in compliance with the SOPs; maintains documentation required by project and corporate SOPs.
* Writes SOPs and workflows to establish new processes. Refines and streamlines these SOPs as processes are implemented. Also writes SOPs for a variety of specialized tasks and suggests changes in project or corporate activities as appropriate.
* Reviews project related reports and makes contributions to appropriate sections.
* Performs other duties as assigned
* Complies with all policies and standards

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's Degree Health related or scientific field and 6 years of related experience Required
* Master's Degree Health related or scientific field and 4 years of related experience Preferred
* Ability to write scientific minutes, particularly related to medical topics. High
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to prepare formal internal and external communications such as reports to clients with minimal assistance. High
* Ability to work both independently and in collaboration with others. High
* Strong computer skills. High
* Strong skills in prioritization, problem solving, organization, decision making, time management, and planning. High
* Ability to exercise judgment within broadly defined practices and policies in selecting methods, techniques and evaluation criteria for obtaining results. High
* Knowledge of clinical trials research preferred. Low
* Experience in a medical and biologic or other health related or clinical research field preferred. Low
* Webpage maintenance skills preferred. Low
* Ability to coach employees and motivate a team. Low

If you’re looking for a career where your work **advances global health** and where **scientific excellence meets real-world impact**, join us and be part of something bigger. **One Team, One Purpose.**  
  
**CONNECT WITH US!**  
*Find us on LinkedIn:/the-emmes-group/*  
Visit our website:https://www.theemmesgroup.com/

title: C-BRAIN Senior Data Scientist (Remote) - Neurology
description:
**Location**
============

Remote, US

**Scheduled Hours**
===================

40

**Position Summary**
====================

The Consortium for Brain Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN) is an academic-industry consortium directed by Dr. Randall J. Bateman, Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. C-BRAIN brings together academic research institutions, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, technology partners, philanthropic organizations, and government agencies to develop AI-powered tools to accelerate discovery in Alzheimer's disease and neurodegenerative disorders. Washington University serves as the coordinating center for C-BRAIN. C-BRAIN is currently deploying initial versions of the tools and developing plans for benchmarking and evaluation of the tools in addition to platform integration and scaling. C-BRAIN is also working on development of foundational AI models for brain aging and neurodegeneration. See www.c-brain.org.
  
  
The C-BRAIN Senior Data Scientist is the team's hands-on expert for the neuroscience research data behind C-BRAIN's models and AI tools, spanning brain imaging, fluid and clinical biomarker data, and spatial proteomic and transcriptomic data from human brain tissue. Reporting to the C-BRAIN Chief Technology Officer (CTO), this role judges whether data are complete and fit for modeling, builds reproducible pipelines that turn raw instrument and study outputs into model-ready datasets, develops and evaluates the models that use them, and runs the automated evaluations and benchmarks that models and AI tools must pass before release to production, working closely with C-BRAIN's foundation-model scientists and engineers.
  
The ideal candidate has worked hands-on with raw neuroscience data in depth (brain imaging, biomarker, or spatial biology data), understands how spatial and imaging data move from instrument to analysis, knows what complete and correct data look like, writes production-quality code, and can lead data and modeling work from day one. This is neither a pipeline-only nor an analysis-only position: data expertise and engineering rigor are equally important. C-BRAIN-specific context will be provided; hands-on data expertise and coding fundamentals will not.

**Job Description**
===================

**Primary Duties & Responsibilities:**

Applied Modeling

* Build and evaluate statistical and machine learning models on spatial omics, brain imaging, biomarker, and clinical data, from strong baselines to deep learning, including cell- and tissue-level, biomarker, and disease-progression models.

* Work with C-BRAIN's Senior Applied Scientist on foundation-model training data, downstream tasks, and embedding analyses that test whether models recover known biology, such as cell types, regional signatures, and age- and disease-related changes.

* Combine data types across studies where it adds signal, including approaches that handle missing modalities and per-dataset expert models, such as tabular expert models trained separately on each contributor's trial, registry, or biomarker data.

Translate questions from researchers into analyses and models, and report results with clear limitations.  



Neuro Data Expertise & Quality

* Serve as the team's hands-on expert for at least one neuroscience data type (brain imaging, fluid and clinical biomarkers, or spatial omics), and apply working knowledge of spatial and imaging data pipelines across the others.

* Judge raw and processed data independently: check instrument exports and study files for completeness (for example, images, segmentation and cell-level outputs, and scanner or assay metadata), identify artifacts and batch or site effects, and decide whether data are fit for modeling.

* Specify what data providers must deliver (data dictionaries, units, assay, panel, and scanner versions, cohort criteria, identifier crosswalks, and QC flags), and follow up when deliveries are incomplete.

* Check contributed data that C-BRAIN staff are not permitted to view: write automated validation and quality reports that run inside the protected environment and release only approved summaries, working from data dictionaries and synthetic data.

* Harmonize data across sites, platforms, and assay versions, and confirm harmonization worked: known biological relationships hold and site cannot be predicted from the data.

Keep current with the literature and with collaborating groups' acquisition and processing methods, and adapt C-BRAIN pipelines and quality checks as methods change.  



Model Evaluation and Benchmarking

* Build and maintain automated evaluation and benchmarking pipelines that every model and AI tool release must pass before production: versioned benchmark datasets, fixed held-out sets, standard metrics, and clear pass/fail thresholds.

* Design evaluations that hold up: subject-level and site-level splits, leakage and contamination checks between training and benchmark data, held-out cohorts, uncertainty estimates, and comparison against simpler methods.

* Develop benchmarks with domain scientists that reflect real research tasks, including recovery of known biology, prediction tasks on spatial, imaging, and biomarker data, and expert-reviewed question sets for AI research tools.

* Evaluate LLM- and agent-based research tools for answer accuracy, grounding and citation quality, and hallucination, using automated scoring checked against expert review, and compare candidate LLMs and agent configurations before the platform changes models.

* Run regression testing across model, data, and provider versions; track performance, calibration, and robustness to site and batch shifts; and report results for release reviews.

Integrate evaluations into CI/CD and model release gates with C-BRAIN engineers, so every result is reproducible and tied to its model, data, and code versions.  



Data Pipelines and Reproducible Code

* Build reproducible pipelines from raw data to model-ready datasets: untouched raw copies, validation and profiling, harmonization, versioned curated data, and data dictionaries.

* Write production-quality Python (and R where needed) with Git, code review, automated tests on code and data, pinned environments, and workflow tools such as Nextflow or Snakemake.

* Run large processing and training jobs on high-performance and cloud computing using containers and schedulers such as Slurm, and track compute cost.

Use AI coding assistants to work faster while verifying generated code with tests and review.  



Technical Leadership and Collaboration

* Lead data and modeling work from day one: run working sessions, set data standards, and review analyses and code.

Mentor data scientists, postdoctoral researchers, and collaborators, and work closely with C-BRAIN engineers, wet-lab, imaging, and clinical scientists, and data contributors.  



Documentation, Governance and Reporting

* Maintain data catalog entries, lineage, and documentation so every dataset and result can be traced and reproduced, including the dataset descriptions shown to consortium researchers with each contributor's consent.

* Provide technical input on data use agreement requirements (formats, transfer, storage, and permitted computation), follow consortium data agreements in all data handling, and apply disclosure checks (for example, minimum cell sizes) to summaries and aggregate results before they leave a protected environment.

Contribute to progress reports, Steering Committee materials, and publications in line with consortium review procedures.  



**Working Conditions**

* Remote within the United States, per current Washington University policies.
* Occasional on-site presence required for team meetings and consortium events.
* Occasional domestic travel may be required for consortium events, partner meetings, or scientific conferences.
* Standard office environment.
* Primarily sedentary with standard computer use.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all job duties performed by the personnel so classified. Management reserves the right to revise or amend duties at any time.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

**Education:**

Master's degree  

**Certifications** **/Professional Licenses** **:**

No specific certification/professional license is required for this position.  

**Work Experience:**

Relevant Experience (5 Years)  

**Skills:**

Not Applicable  

**Driver's License:**

A driver's license is not required for this position.

**More About This Job**
=======================

**Required Qualifications**

* Master's degree in data science, neuroscience, biomedical engineering, computational biology, bioinformatics, biostatistics, computer science, or a related field.

* Five years of research or professional experience analyzing and modeling biomedical data; doctoral research may count toward this experience.

* Deep hands-on experience with at least one neuroscience data type (brain imaging such as MRI or PET, fluid or clinical biomarker data, or spatial proteomics or transcriptomics), including processing and quality-checking raw data through to analysis-ready data.

* Basic working understanding of spatial omics and imaging data pipelines, such as how tissue images become segmented cells and cell-level measurements, sufficient to judge whether such data are complete and fit for use.

* Production-quality Python with Git, code review, and automated testing.

* Demonstrated experience building, validating, and benchmarking predictive or representation models, including subject-level validation, leakage prevention, and automated, reproducible evaluation.

* Experience harmonizing data from multiple sites, studies, or platforms.

* Experience leading or mentoring others on technical work.

Work you can walk through in detail: code repositories, publications, or analyses (described at a high level if proprietary).  



**Preferred Qualifications**

* PhD in neuroscience, computational biology, biomedical engineering, biostatistics, computer science, or a related field.

* Hands-on spatial omics expertise, including cell segmentation and image processing, on platforms such as CosMx, Xenium, MERFISH, CODEX, or imaging mass cytometry, with tools such as Squidpy, SpatialData, the scverse ecosystem, Cellpose, or CellProfiler.

* Brain imaging (MRI or PET) processing with tools such as FreeSurfer, FSL, ANTs, or fMRIPrep, and formats such as DICOM, NIfTI, and BIDS.

* Fluid and clinical biomarker data (for example, plasma or CSF assays and large-scale proteomics) and longitudinal clinical and cognitive data.

* Alzheimer's disease and neurodegeneration research cohorts and data repositories.

* Deep learning on images or high-dimensional data with PyTorch, including working with foundation-model embeddings.

* Evaluation and experiment tooling for machine learning and LLM systems (for example, MLflow or Weights & Biases, and LLM evaluation harnesses), and building evaluations into CI/CD release gates.

* Multimodal, mixture-of-experts, missing-modality, or longitudinal modeling methods.

* Federated learning, privacy-preserving analysis, or work inside secure computing environments.

* GPU-accelerated analysis (for example, RAPIDS or cuCIM) and HPC environments with Slurm and containers.

* Experience in research consortia or with data governed by data use agreements.

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

**Education:**

Ph.D. - Doctor of Philosophy  

**Certifications** **/Professional Licenses** **:**

No additional certification/professional licenses unless stated elsewhere in the job posting.  

**Work Experience:**

No additional work experience unless stated elsewhere in the job posting.

**Skills:**

Artificial Intelligence (AI), Code Reviews, Communication, Data Harmonization, Data Management, Data Modeling, Data Quality Assessments, Git, Neuroscience, Peer Collaboration, Production Quality, Professional Judgement, Reproducible Research, Spatial Visualization, Statistical Data, Team Collaboration, Technical Leadership

**Grade**
=========

G16

**Salary Range**
================

$96,000.00 - $169,300.00 / AnnuallyThe salary range reflects base salaries paid for positions in a given job grade across the University. Individual rates within the range will be determined by factors including one's qualifications and performance, equity with others in the department, market rates for positions within the same grade and department budget.

**Questions**
=============

For frequently asked questions about the application process, please refer to our External Applicant FAQ .

**Accommodation**
=================

If you are unable to use our online application system and would like an accommodation, please email CandidateQuestions@wustl.edu or call the dedicated accommodation inquiry number at 314-935-1149 and leave a voicemail with the nature of your request.

All qualified individuals must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily and, if requested, reasonable accommodations will be made to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their job, absent undue hardship.

**Pre-Employment Screening**
============================

All external candidates receiving an offer for employment will be required to submit to pre-employment screening for this position. The screenings will include criminal background check and, as applicable for the position, other background checks, drug screen, an employment and education or licensure/certification verification, physical examination, certain vaccinations and/or governmental registry checks. All offers are contingent upon successful completion of required screening.

**Benefits Statement**
======================

Personal

* Up to 22 days of vacation, 10 recognized holidays, and sick time.
* Competitive health insurance packages with priority appointments and lower copays/coinsurance.
* Take advantage of our free Metro transit U-Pass for eligible employees.
* WashU provides eligible employees with a defined contribution (403(b)) Retirement Savings Plan, which combines employee contributions and university contributions starting at 7%.

Wellness

* Wellness challenges, annual health screenings, mental health resources, mindfulness programs and courses, employee assistance program (EAP), financial resources, access to dietitians, and more!

Family

* We offer 4 weeks of caregiver leave to bond with your new child. Family care resources are also available for your continued childcare needs. Need adult care? We’ve got you covered.
* WashU covers the cost of tuition for you and your family, including dependent undergraduate-level college tuition up to 100% at WashU and 40% elsewhere after seven years with us.

For policies, detailed benefits, and eligibility, please visit: https://hr.wustl.edu/benefits/

**EEO Statement**

It is the University’s policy to provide equal opportunity and access to persons in all job titles without regard to race, ethnicity or shared ancestry, color, national origin, citizenship (where prohibited by federal law), age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information.
